name: mcpelevator
description: Elevate MCP servers into authenticated HTTP endpoints - self-hosted, in one container. Most MCP servers ship as stdio programs (npx/uvx commands) that phones and remote clients can't spawn. mcpelevator runs them for you and exposes each as a remote Streamable HTTP endpoint that Claude mobile (or any MCP client) on your network can connect to: add a server in the web UI, press start, copy the URL. Batteries included (Node/npx + Python/uv preinstalled), with process supervision, live logs, a registry browser for one-click installs, bearer-token auth, and a Host/Origin guard. Already-remote MCP servers can be proxied behind the same auth too. DOCKER RUNNER (advanced, opt-in, requires mcpelevator 1.1.0+): mcpelevator can also run MCP servers packaged as Docker images. It is OFF by default and ROOT-EQUIVALENT - to use it, set the Docker Runner variable to true AND give it a Docker endpoint, EITHER by adding a Path mapping /var/run/docker.sock -> /var/run/docker.sock (sibling model, hands the host daemon to mcpelevator) OR by setting the Docker Host variable to a separate dind daemon (stronger isolation, no host-socket mount; because this container uses HOST networking, point Docker Host at localhost or the host IP where dind publishes its port, NOT a container name like 'dind'). The docker runner and CLI ship in 1.1.0 - on an older image the toggle does nothing. See the Unraid guide for the walkthrough. FIRST LOGIN: this template enables LAN access, which turns control-plane auth on - the admin token is minted on first start and printed ONCE to the container log. Open the log, copy the token, and log in at http:// :8080. Host networking is used so the LAN-access gate sees real client IPs (with bridge + port publishing every client would look like the Docker gateway). Full guide: https://github.com/pacnpal/mcpelevator/blob/main/docs/Unraid.md

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Persistent data: SQLite database (servers, tokens, settings) and the npm/uv package caches so installed MCP servers survive restarts.

variables.name: WebUI Port
variables.description: Port the control plane binds on the host. Host networking has no port mapping, so this variable IS the host port - change it if 8080 is already taken, and update the container's WebUI field to match so the WebUI link keeps working.

variables.name: Allow LAN Access
variables.description: First-boot seed for the 'allow access from devices on your local network' setting, so this headless box is reachable at http:// :8080 right away. Enabling it turns control-plane auth ON: the admin token is printed ONCE to the container log on first start - copy it there to log in. Only seeds the first boot; the toggle in Settings is authoritative afterwards.

variables.name: Admin Token (break-glass)
variables.description: Optional. A control-plane token that is always accepted on /api. Leave empty normally (a token is minted and printed to the log on first start); set it to recover from a lost token or for automation, then remove it.

variables.name: Public Base URL
variables.description: Optional. Absolute URL clients use to reach this instance when it sits behind a tunnel or reverse proxy (e.g. https://mcp.example.com). The copy menu hands out endpoint URLs based on it, and its hostname is trusted by the Host/Origin guard.

variables.name: Extra Allowed Hosts
variables.description: Optional. Comma-separated extra hostnames the Host/Origin guard always trusts (e.g. a reverse-proxy hostname that resolves to this box). Not needed for plain LAN access by IP.

variables.name: Docker Runner (root-equivalent)
variables.description: OPT-IN and ROOT-EQUIVALENT. Requires mcpelevator 1.1.0 or newer (the docker runner and CLI ship in 1.1.0; on an older image this toggle does nothing). First-boot seed for the docker runner, which launches MCP servers packaged as Docker images on a mounted Docker daemon. Anything that can reach the Docker socket is effectively root on the host, so enable this only if you trust every image you run. It needs a Docker endpoint - EITHER add a Path mount manually (click 'Add another Path, Port, Variable...' at the bottom of this page) with Container Path and Host Path both set to /var/run/docker.sock (sibling-container model), OR set the 'Docker Host' variable below to a separate dind daemon (stronger isolation, no host-socket mount). OFF by default; the Settings toggle is authoritative after first boot.

variables.name: Docker Host (docker runner, optional)
variables.description: Optional, and only used by the Docker Runner. Leave EMPTY for the sibling model - the runner then uses the mounted /var/run/docker.sock (empty behaves exactly like unset; no effect). Set it to a separate/dind daemon endpoint (e.g. tcp://localhost:2375) to run launched images on that daemon instead of the host's, so images never touch Unraid's own Docker (stronger isolation, no host-socket mount). NOTE: this container uses HOST networking, so it can't resolve Docker service names like 'dind' - point it at localhost or the host's IP where the dind container publishes its port. SECURITY: a plaintext tcp://...:2375 endpoint is unauthenticated and root-equivalent - only use it on a strictly private, non-routable network and never publish it; for anything less contained front dind with TLS on 2376.

variables.name: Mint Admin Token On Boot
variables.description: Recovery hatch: set to true to mint a fresh admin token on boot and print it to the container log (existing tokens keep working). Set back to false after grabbing it, or a new token is minted on every restart.

variables.name: Max Running Servers
variables.description: Cap on concurrently running MCP servers.

variables.name: Start Timeout (seconds)
variables.description: Readiness timeout per server start - generous by default to cover npx/uvx cold-start package installs. Raise it for very large packages.
